prerequisites: To enroll in this course, it is necessary to have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses lower than the one in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the technological basis on which the most recent research in thermal engines is supported.
Know the types, operation, and applications of thermal machines and engines.
Provide explanations about the environmental and sustainability implications of a given problem.
Solve problems inherent to thermal machines, both mechanical and related to pollutant emissions.
Perform experimental analyses to evaluate the characteristic operating curves of thermal engines under different load conditions.
Perform designs, calculations, and tests, justifying their results, drawing conclusions, and writing reports on them.
Know and calculate boilers, burners, furnaces, and dryers.
Delve into techniques for utilizing fossil fuels and renewable fuels for use in boilers.
Understand the basic aspects of a heat pump.
Know and calculate the thermodynamic properties and processes of refrigerants.
Know cold production systems and their design and calculation.
Study the processes and equipment of various systems used for the conversion or utilization of renewable energies into heat.

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is the default. Partial exams allow students to cover course content, with failed partials recoverable in the first opportunity final exam, otherwise, the student must take the full exam in the second opportunity. Lab practice deliverables account for 10% of the continuous assessment, and supervised work for another 10%, with the final exam (80%) covering other topics. Grades from supervised work and practices are added only after the final exam or all partials are passed; if the average without these is above 5 but not all exams are passed, the final grade is 4.9. For single assessment, students can opt out of continuous assessment and take a 100% final exam covering all topics. A resit exam is available for students who do not pass the first opportunity, and prior practice and work grades can be retained. Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a global failing grade of 0.0.
